title: Stitch notes: runbook for customer requests and engineering hooks
content:
Purpose:
This is a working runbook + annotated request ledger to translate recurring customer asks (Q1–Q2 2025) into tractable engineering hooks. Aim: have a single digestible artifact product, infra, and SRE teams can use to prioritize low-friction patches and medium-effort changes that reduce customer pain and outage risk.

Context / why this doc now:
- Recent spike in field reports around KV cache invalidations, streaming disconnects, and confusion around Dedicated vs Hosted quotas. Several mid-market customers have raised churn risk (accounts flagged in JIRA-RED-4821).
- CS has been triaging on Slack and creating ad-hoc tickets; engineering asked for a consolidated set of reproducible behaviors + suggested mitigations.

How to use this runbook:
- Read the quick triage summary for each theme, then scan the action rows at the end.
- For each action, an owner is suggested; owners should convert to an engineering ticket with acceptance criteria and estimated effort.

Quick triage summary (themes):
1) KV cache friction (prefix cache misses, stale tokens)
   - Customer impact: elevated latency for multi-turn chat after short idle periods; increased token cost due to repeated recomputation.
   - Signals: customer logs show rapid cache evictions when sequence length distribution spikes; SRE found a 20% increase in cold-starts for chat pods during business hours.
   - Example quote: "After 30s of inactivity the chat goes cold and the cost doubles — our user flows are very conversational." — Large SaaS customer (Account: AcmeAI)

2) Streaming disconnects and resume behavior
   - Customer impact: partial responses, clients re-issuing requests and duplicating tokens.
   - Signals: mobile clients (iOS) report disconnects when cellular handoff occurs; backend logs show socket close without clear error codes.
   - Local workaround: instruct clients to use idempotency keys + client-side merge logic.

3) Rollout confusion: model variants & fallback routing
   - Customer impact: customers pinned to a model saw silent fallback to lower-capacity variant during bursts; unexpected regression in output quality.
   - Signals: several support threads referencing "sudden tone change" and linked to model-switch timestamps.

4) Private deployment onboarding friction (VPC & KMS integration)
   - Customer impact: enterprise customers delayed go-live for weeks due to unclear KMS permissions and audit log format differences vs hosted.
   - Signals: professional services tickets show repetitive steps in the onboarding playbook.

5) Billing / metrology clarity (token accounting for streaming + retries)
   - Customer impact: customers seeing higher-than-expected bills after implementing retry logic.
   - Signals: billing inquiries spike following incident windows where streaming disconnects were frequent.

Requests & suggested engineering hooks (annotated):
- KV cache: introduce a "soft-ttl" telemetry flag + eviction debug endpoint (Effort: S-M) — owner: Evan Kim. Acceptance: endpoint returns per-model per-pool eviction stats; we can reproduce customer sequence with synthetic workload. Linked: JIRA-RED-4821.
- Streaming: add socket-level close reason logging + client resume protocol sample (Effort: M) — owner: Sofia Chen. Acceptance: close codes captured in logs and surfaced to Console; sample iOS client added to SDK repo (GH-PR-1204).
- Rollout transparency: expose model-fallback audit events to the Console with a small UI (Effort: M-L; UI+backend) — owner: Miguel Ramirez. Acceptance: Console shows timestamped fallback events and the variant that served each request.
- Private onboarding: consolidate KMS steps into a scripted checklist (bash/terraform snippets) and add to the PS repo (Effort: S) — owner: Priya Nair. Acceptance: PS time-to-first-successful-call reduced from ~10d to <=3d in playbook dry-run.
- Billing: publish a short billing note that clarifies streaming token boundaries & best-practice idempotency to avoid duplicate charges (Effort: XS) — owner: Asha Patel (CS). Acceptance: documentation live; copy sent to 3 affected customers for validation.

Risk triage and cost-impact notes:
- High-risk/High-impact: model fallback transparency. Blind fallback can cause quality regressions and contracts. Prioritize as P0 for customers on Dedicated SLA.
- Medium-risk: KV cache tuning. Remediations can reduce per-token cost significantly for chat-heavy customers; quantify savings in next sprint.
- Low-risk: billing doc. Low engineering cost, high customer confidence value.

Open questions / unresolved:
- Are we comfortable exposing per-request variant data in Console without leaking internal placement? (Privacy/obfuscation question for Infra & Security).
- For streaming resume, should the protocol be maintained entirely client-side or do we implement a light server-side resume token? Need infra input on statefulness tradeoffs.

Immediate next steps (next 2 sprints):
- Sprint 1 (owners above): create engineering tickets with acceptance criteria and rough estimates by 2025-05-09.
- Sprint 2: land KV cache debug endpoint + first-pass streaming close-code logging.
- Parallel: Asha to draft billing note and gather validation from 3 customers by 2025-05-12.

Small reproducible experiments (for eng):
- Synthetic chat workload: 60s idle/5-turn resume pattern to reproduce KV cold-starts. Test matrix: batch sizes (1,4,8), seq lengths (128/512/1024).
- Mobile streaming stress: simulate 4G->LTE handoff events and measure socket lifecycle; capture server close codes.

Ticket triage template (to paste into new tickets):
- Title: [CS-STITCH] short descriptor (e.g., KV-cache eviction debug endpoint)
- Background: short customer story + link to customer ticket(s)
- Reproduction steps: exact curl/SDK steps used in repro
- Acceptance criteria: measurable checks (logs, Console view, test harness pass)
- Estimated effort (XS/S/M/L) and proposed owner

Action items (owner & due):
- Asha: draft billing note and send to validation customers (due 2025-05-12).
- Evan: create KV cache ticket with debug endpoint spec (due 2025-05-09).
- Sofia: prototype streaming close-code logging change and open GH-PR (due 2025-05-09).
- Miguel: wireframe fallback events in Console and sync with Security (due 2025-05-16).
- Priya: assemble KMS onboarding snippets and PS checklist (due 2025-05-09).

Notes to self (CS):
- Keep one-line customer summaries attached to tickets so engineering has context.
- Avoid shipping Console data that directly maps to internal hostnames. Use anonymized IDs.

Appendix: sample customer snippets (redacted)
- "We started seeing the model change tone last week — not sure what changed on your end, but our users are noticing." — mid-market fintech
- "Streaming dropped three times during a 10-minute session; our users retried and that doubled our bill." — enterprise analytics platform

If you’re reading and want to add a thread: comment here, @mention an owner, and we’ll convert to a ticket. This doc is intentionally a lightweight bridge between field signal and sprintable engineering work.

-- Asha (on behalf of CS runtime triage)
